impl:threats-live.summary:
Predators now hunt in real worlds. On the five round-3 hand-over snapshots (seed 1, one per archetype, 6 game days, Naturalist) every stage of every predator family read 0 before the change. Root causes, each shown by a funnel count and a test:
C1. Worldgen put every hunting predator's territory 511-3,000 BU from the nest. The colonies' ants stay within about 100-220 BU (90th percentile).
C2. Ants fled from any predator within 6 BU (24 mm), including hidden ones, dormant ones and buried antlions. Strike ranges are 6-16 mm, so no predator ever got close enough to strike. GDD 05 §2.4 sets detection at 4 L x stealth.
C3. Rove beetles hunted only at night; GDD §2.2a says they are also active by day in leaf litter.
C4. The ant-spider approached at 6 mm/s, a code constant slower than any walking ant.
C5. Small colonies never raised a `predator-near` alert, because the rule needs 3 foragers within 15 BU of the predator.
C6. The possessed ant got no `possessed-danger` card for "seized" or "stuck".
Not defects: zero bird visits is the GDD rule (birds only target colonies of 30 or more workers), and none of the 5 worlds has antlion habitat.

Fixes, all inside the creature module except one 3-line edit to ant perception:
- After the hand-over, the director places one territory for each hunting kind that has habitat within 40-140 BU of the entrance, near the routes to food. Capped places are filled nearest the colony first.
- Ants now detect predators at the GDD 05 §2.4 range.
- Rove beetles also hunt by day in litter; the ant-spider approaches at the GDD walk speed of 15 mm/s.
- A landed strike raises `predator-near`; `possessed-danger` is raised for "seized" and "stuck".
- Lowering the Predators setting (or turning it off) mid-game now removes the extra predators within 1 game day (GDD 06 §14).

Measured worker deaths to predators per outside-worker game day: Gentle 0.01, Naturalist 0.07, Harsh 0.16, Off 0. The target band is derived from GDD 02 §1.3 (0.061 per outside-worker game day), and all three presets fall inside it in the right order.

Cost to colonies, from the forage bench run to winter on the same 5 snapshots: 14 workers lost to predators across the 5 colonies, 56 → 39 workers at winter, trips down 27 %. That is about 3 workers per colony of 12-16. This follows from the design's own arithmetic, so I did not rebalance; the report lists three one-constant levers for the integrator.

Per-tick cost of the creature systems: 0.34 → 0.30 ms at 60 workers and 0.34 → 0.40 ms at 300 workers, under the 0.2 ms regression limit (machine load 10-11).

Browser harness: a jumping spider placed by the colony telegraphs and strikes a possessed worker. I looked at all three screenshots and they show the wind-up, the leap with the "Predator near foragers" card, and an observer close-up.

Partial: AC2 is not fully met. Jumping spiders reached strike on 0 of 5 worlds in the final run (2 of 5 in an earlier round and on Harsh). Rove beetles reached it on 1 of 5. Centipedes have habitat on only 2 of 5 worlds and struck on 1.

findings.title: AC2 not met: three hunting families reach 'strike' on fewer than 3 of 5 worlds, and the reason given is not 'no habitat'
findings.where: docs/design/tasks/threats-live-report.md §2.1 and §11; src/sim/ecology/creatures/spiders.ts (jumping-spider stalk/windup gate), hunters.ts (rove beetle)
findings.detail: AC2 allows a family to miss 3 of 5 only when that archetype has no habitat for it. Final run (after3): jumping spider struck on 0/5 worlds although it was sited on 4/5 and sensed ants on 4/5; ant-spider 2/5; rove beetle 1/5, sited on 5/5. The implementer's own explanation is behavioural: the stalk at 8 mm/s never closes on a cruising ant, and the wind-up only starts on an ant moving slower than 6.7 mm/s. That is not a habitat reason. The centipede (habitat on 2/5, struck on 1) and the antlion (no habitat on any world) are acceptable. The implementer reports this honestly as 'partial'. It still blocks AC2 and should go back with the lead the report already names (site jumping spiders on food-host stems where ants stop).

findings.title: The colony-range siting memo is runtime-only, so after a Predators setting change a reload diverges from the uninterrupted game, and the raised setting adds nothing until a reload
findings.where: src/sim/ecology/creatures/colonyRange.ts:150-172 (const settled = new WeakMap; memo.kinds.add(kind) before colonyRangeDrawn)
findings.detail: ensureColonyRangeTerritories marks each kind as settled in a per-Sim WeakMap before it checks colonyRangeDrawn(sim, kind), and that check depends on the current Predators setting. On a world where a kind is not drawn at Few, raising the setting Few -> Normal mid-game never sites that kind in the running game, because the memo already says it is settled. After a save -> load the memo is empty, so the kind is sited at once. Two problems follow. (a) A reload changes the simulation, against AC4 and the design seed's determinism rule. (b) It breaks GDD 06 §14 ('adding threats spawns them at the normal rate'). Reproduction: threatsLive.verify.test.ts 'raising Few -> Normal sites the same territories in the running game as after a save -> load' FAILS: the reloaded sim's territory list differs from the running sim's. Its precondition test passes, so at least one kind on woodland-edge #1 is drawn at Normal but not at Few. Fix direction: memoise only the kinds that are actually settled for the current setting (or key the memo by setting), so both paths take the same decision.

findings.title: Resident rebalance churns: a far resident is despawned and respawned on every director run while the near colony site cannot be filled
findings.detail: rebalanceResidents despawns the farthest unseen resident whenever a nearer territory of the same kind is free. It does not check that the near territory can actually be filled now. When spawnPointOk fails (an ant within 20 BU of the site centre, or a possessed ant within 40 BU), occupyTerritories skips the near site and refills a far territory. The next run does the same again. Reproduction: threatsLive.verify.test.ts 'a far resident is not despawned and respawned over and over while an ant stands on the near site' FAILS with 19 'rebalanced' despawns in 20 director runs (1000 ticks). On the woodland-edge snapshot with AI play only, it happened once per game day. It becomes continuous when the player keeps a possessed ant near a free colony-range site. Each cycle allocates a creature and emits spawn and despawn events. Nothing visible happens, because farFromFocus protects residents in view. Fix: rebalance only when the near site passes spawnPointOk (and its surface check) in the same run.

findings.title: possessed-danger 'seized' overwrites combat's 'pinned' card, then clears it while the ant is still pinned
findings.detail: Alerts are keyed by kind and subject. When a card from another module already exists (combat 'pinned', flood 'under-water'), possessedDangerAlerts calls raiseAlert anyway, which overwrites cause and title with 'seized'. When the seize ends, its clear loop removes the card because the cause no longer matches. Combat has already set its PIN_ON flag, so it does not raise the card again, and a pinned possessed ant is left with no critical card. Reproduction: threatsLive.verify.test.ts 'a pinned ant keeps a possessed-danger card after a predator lets go of her' FAILS (card undefined). The flood module solves the same problem by leaving a card raised by another module alone (nest/flood/diagnostics.ts possessedFloodAlert). This is a rare combination (pinned and seized at once).

findings.title: Pre-existing in the owned director: jumping-spider and rove-beetle worldgen territories whose centre is inside a solid are retried every director run
findings.detail: Probe on the woodland-edge round-3 snapshot at Naturalist: 240 jumping-spider spawns per game day, each despawned at once with cause 'no-surface', and 33 per game day for rove beetles. The causes are territories 319 and 320 (field at the centre -85 and -35 mm) and rove territories 32, 33 and 35. The kind stays below its cap, so every run tries them again. The 'before' funnel JSONs show the same total despawn counts, so the change did not introduce this, but it lives in the owned module and costs allocations and events every 5 s. Fix: mark a territory whose spawn fails as vacant for a while, or drop it.

findings.title: Jumping-spider site height ignores primitive rotation, so lying logs and boards count as vertical surfaces
findings.detail: objectRise uses pos.y + size.y for each primitive. size holds half-extents in the primitive's local frame (types/geom.ts), so the rotation is ignored and VISUAL_ONLY primitives are included. A horizontal cylinder (a fallen log) or a rotated capsule reports its half-length as height and passes the 40 mm 'vertical surface' test, which goes against GDD 05 §2.2b ('vertical sunny surfaces'). Also, the site is the object's centre at ground height, which is usually inside the object. On woodland-edge the colony jumping-spider site has field -0.9 mm and only works because placeOnSurface projects it out.

findings.title: The 'stuck' sub-cause is used for ant-spider paralysis; in GDD 05, 'stuck' is the spill-trap state
findings.detail: GDD 05 §1 (spill drowning) and §4 list 'paralysed' and 'stuck' as separate states, each with its own event (ant-paralysed and ant-stuck). The card raises cause 'stuck' with the title 'Paralysed', so diagnostics or UI that filter on cause 'stuck' would read paralysis as a spill trap. Use cause 'paralysed', or record this as a GDD reading in the report.

findings.title: AC3 bands are the implementer's own derivation, and the Gentle, Harsh and off tables predate the final code
findings.detail: The GDD states no loss band. The 0.061 per outside-worker game day derived from GDD 02 §1.3 is reasonable, but the Gentle (<= 0.06) and Harsh (0.06-0.2) bands are invented. The Naturalist rate (0.07) rests on 7 kills in one run per world, and two of five worlds had 0. The Gentle, Harsh and off runs were made before settingCull was added and were not repeated. My 1-game-day off run on woodland-edge is consistent (0 events, residents gone). The integrator should treat AC3 as 'consistent with the design arithmetic', not as met against a GDD band.

fix:threats-live.summary:
I reproduced all 8 reviewer findings. Six had code fixes, one needed a GDD reading, and AC2 went from partial to better but still partial. The six code fixes:
- Memo/reload divergence: the runtime memo is gone and siting now runs on the director's hourly runs. The creature conditions cache had a second cause, which is also fixed.
- Rebalance churn: fixed.
- Pinned card overwritten by "seized": fixed.
- Placement retries every run: territories whose resident cannot be placed now wait 1 game day. Spawn and despawn events fell 90-94 %.
- Jumping-spider height ignored rotation: the vertical-surface test now applies the rotation.
- Paralysis was raised under the spill-trap cause "stuck": the cause is now `paralysed`.

All 6 reviewer tests pass, with one assertion adapted, and I added tests for each fix.

For AC2, predators only strike an ant that pauses, so I now site them where ants stop:
- The jumping spider and the rove beetle are sited at the colony's nearest food sources.
- The jumping spider goes on the food stems themselves, with an inner ring edge of 20 BU instead of 40.
- A blocked territory may now spawn its resident at 8 nearby points and let it walk home.

In the final Naturalist run the jumping spider and the ant-spider struck on 5 of 5 worlds. Wolf spider (2 of 5 in the final run, 2-3 of 5 in fix2-fix4, 4 of 5 at review) and rove beetle (2-4 of 5) still vary from run to run. The centipede struck on 1 of its 2 habitat worlds (2 of 2 in fix3).

The cost is a much higher loss rate: 0.40 deaths per outside-worker game day on Naturalist, against the design's 0.061. The 5 colonies dropped from 69 to 32 workers in 6 game days. Gentle is 0.02, Harsh 0.45, and Predators off gives 0. I report this conflict and the levers in the report, section 12.4, without rebalancing, as the spec's step 5 requires. Typecheck is clean. The creatures and perception tests pass (27 files, 184 passed). I looked at the harness screenshots. There was no per-tick cost regression.

(a) The runtime WeakMap memo in colonyRange.ts is removed; siting is now a function of saved state only and the director calls it on its hourly runs, which are persisted through lastHourlyTick. (b) The conditions() cache in conditions.ts was keyed by tick only; it is now also keyed by the identity of the difficulty preset, params, custom settings and rules.
